title: The KŁR conjecture on sparse regular graphs
statement:
Let $H$) be a fixed graph with vertex set $\{1,2,\dots,k\}$. For positive integers $n,m$ and positive reals $p,\epsilon$, let $\mathcal{G}(H,n,m,p,\epsilon)$ be the collection of graphs whose vertex set is a disjoint union $V_1\cup\cdots\cup V_k$ of sets of size $n$, with an $(\epsilon,p)$-regular bipartite graph having $m$ edges between $V_i$ and $V_j$ for every $ij\in E(H)$ and no other edges. Let $\mathcal{G}^*(H,n,m,p,\epsilon)$ be the graphs in this collection containing no canonical copy of $H$, and let $m_2(H)$ denote the 2-density of $H$. **KŁR conjecture.** For every fixed graph $H$ and every $\beta>0$, there exist $C,\epsilon>0$ and a positive integer $n_0$ such that

$$
|\mathcal{G}^*(H,n,m,m/n^2,\epsilon)|\leq \beta^m\binom{n^2}{m}^{e(H)}
$$

for every $n\geq n_0$ and every $m\geq Cn^{2-1/m_2(H)}$. The conjecture asserts that the bad graphs form an exponentially small fraction of all graphs with $m$ edges across each edge-pair of $H$, which would enable a union-bound argument in sparse embedding problems.
source_name: D. Conlon, W. T. Gowers, W. Samotij and M. Schacht, “On the KŁR conjecture in random graphs”, arXiv:1305.2516 (2013).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1305.2516

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2013).
